title: Photo Headline
description: Photo-led ad: one product claim told by a photo, with a big headline, a subline and a demo CTA. Three designs (Full Photo, Photo Bottom, Split) in two themes (Royal Blue, Navy).
useWhen: The message is one product claim a photo can carry: the problem, the result, or a before and after.
notWhen: A person is the message (ae-spotlight), or the piece announces an event.
guidance: Designs: full-photo (default) puts the headline on navy over a full-frame photo; photo-bottom puts headline and subline on the gradient above the photo; split shows two photos side by side with a label on each (a before and after, or any comparison). Themes: royal (default), navy. Use the default unless the requester asks for another or for options; for options, render two or three designs in the same set.
headline: one claim, at most two lines (about 22 characters per line). Short copy grows to fill the column. A line break in the copy is fine ("Full schedule.\nFrozen server.").
subline: one line, about 48 characters. Leave it out if there is none; the column closes up.
cta: the button label, about 24 characters ("Book a demo").
image-photo (full-photo, photo-bottom): a real scene that shows the claim, landscape or square, subject near the centre. It is cropped to the frame (tall on Stories).

image-left and image-right (split only): the two photos compared; both are needed for split. label-left and label-right: one or two words each ("Before", "After"); leave them out when there is no comparison.
Photos come from the requester or the team's approved ad photos. Never invent a scene that misstates the product.
